summary: Ganesh Prasad was an Indian scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the University of Allahabad (c. 1893–1897) and University of Calcutta (c. 1897–1898), later holding posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Calcutta, and Banaras Hindu University.

Ganganatha Jha was an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Calcutta, Allahabad, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. His career included posts at Raj Darbhanga, Muir Central College, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (Principal), and the University of Allahabad (Vice Chancellor).

Gangzhun is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Qinghai Nationalities University until 1989 and earned a master's degree at Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001) under the supervision of Alak Dorje Rinpoche.

Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Hanna Havnevik and Lama Byambaa, earning an M.Phil. in Tibetan Studies from the University of Oslo (attested 2008).
Garab Dorje Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

Garcin de Tassy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Collège de France under Jean-Daniel Kieffer and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He was a founder of the Société Asiatique and long held a chair at INALCO.

Gareth Fisher works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned a Ph.D. in socio-cultural anthropology from the University of Virginia (2006) and served as Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).

Gareth Sparham is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at McGill, the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and UBC under Ashok Aklujkar, later teaching at UBC, the University of Michigan, and UC Berkeley.

Gary A. Tubb is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held faculty posts at Harvard University (c. 1979–1986), Columbia University (c. 1999–2007), and the University of Chicago (from c. 2007).

Gary D. DeAngelis is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy who studied under mentors Masatoshi Nagatomi and W. J. Johnson. He served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).

Gary Snyder is a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and general scholar. He studied at Reed College, Indiana University, and UC Berkeley under Shih-Hsiang Chen, later serving on the faculty at UC Davis (1986–2002) and UC Irvine.

Gary Urton is an archaeologist and anthropologist who studied at Eastern New Mexico University, the University of New Mexico, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. He held faculty appointments at Colgate University (1978–2002) and Harvard University (2012–2020).

Gaspare Gorresio studied at the University of Turin, with Eugène Burnouf, and with Stanislas Julien. He held a chair in Sanskrit at the University of Turin from 1852 and served as director of the National University Library of Turin.

Gaston Paris was a French linguist who studied under Friedrich Christian Diez and at the École des chartes. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (c. 1868–1903) and the Collège de France (1872–1903).
Gaston Renondeau was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Polytechnique from c. 1899 to 1901.

Gaton Ngawang Lekpa was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and Tibetologist who studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, later teaching Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and Khenpo Shenga.

Gauri Viswanathan is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Delhi and Columbia University. She taught English at Delhi (c. 1973–1978) before becoming Class of 1933 Professor in the Humanities at Columbia (c. 1989).

Gaurinath Sastri was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (c. 1957–1969), Philological Secretary of The Asiatic Society (attested 1959), and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (c. 1976–1979).

Gavin D'Costa is a religious studies scholar who studied at the universities of Cambridge and Birmingham. He taught at the West London Institute of Higher Education and was appointed at the University of Bristol in 1993.

Gavin Flood is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. He held posts at Wales (Lampeter), Stirling, the University of Oxford, and Yale-NUS College.
